Tool call

One call a tool was asked to make, through its whole life: a line that is always in view with the status in words, a plain summary and the time, the arguments and output behind one disclosure, and Allow and Decline while it waits for approval.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For every tool call in a transcript, as the content of a message row of the tool-call kind, with the row modifier.
  • For the steps inside a step group, with the same markup.
  • On its own as a card, in an activity view or a run's detail view.

When not to use it

  • For a request that needs the reader's full attention before it is answered: its risk, where it runs, a note back to the agent. Use an approval. The row's Allow and Decline are for a request the reader can judge from its one line and its arguments.
  • For several calls summed up in one line. Use a step group, which holds these rows.
  • For a one-line record of what an agent did, among other events. Use an activity feed entry.
  • For the agent's reasoning. Use reasoning, beside the rows and never inside one.

Variants

card
The default: a framed card, for a call that stands alone.
row ds-tool-call--row
No frame. For the content of a ds-message ds-message--tool-call row in a transcript, and for a step in a step group. This is the one way to show a tool call in a transcript.
succeeded, earlier form ds-tool-call--succeeded
Markup written before data-state existed: an outcome class on a root with no data-state, a heading in ds-tool-call__title holding ds-tool-call__name, a status line in ds-tool-call__meta and a details element each for arguments and output. It is drawn as before. New markup sets data-state="succeeded" instead.
failed, earlier form ds-tool-call--failed
The earlier form of data-state="failed".
denied, earlier form ds-tool-call--denied
The earlier form of data-state="declined". Its running state was aria-busy="true" on the root.

Accessibility

  • The app sets data-state on the root and changes it as the call moves on: requested while the arguments are still arriving, awaiting-approval, running, then one final state: succeeded, failed, declined when a person or a rule refused it, timed-out, or cancelled when it was superseded or stopped before it ran. A final state never changes again. The stylesheet draws the icon from data-state and nothing else, so no class is toggled.
  • A retry is a new row after the failed one. Never set a failed row back to running: the reader would lose the failure and its output.
  • The root is an article with aria-labelledby pointing at ds-tool-call__title when it stands alone, and a div with the row modifier inside the li of a transcript or a step group.
  • The line is the summary of one native details element, ds-tool-call__details. It holds ds-tool-call__title, which starts with ds-tool-call__status and goes on with the summary, then ds-tool-call__duration. Enter and Space open and close it. It is drawn 36px tall, to keep a long run dense, and its pointer target is 44px tall.
  • ds-tool-call__status always holds a word, written by the app: Preparing, Awaiting approval, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Declined (or Denied when a permission rule refused it), Timed out, Cancelled. The icon is never the only sign. The one exception is drawn by the stylesheet, not the markup: in the list of an open step group, the word Succeeded is cut from view and only its check shows, because the group's summary says the steps went well. It stays in the text, so a screen reader still reads it; write it as in every other row. Only the running icon moves, and under prefers-reduced-motion it is still. The states the badge's status set names look as it gives them: awaiting-approval is Needs input, running is Working, failed is Check failed and cancelled is Cancelled. Timed-out takes a clock and the warning tone, as a timed-out check does, because it is not a failure of the call.
  • The summary is app text in plain words with the command or the target in a code element with ds-tool-call__target: Ran npm test, Edited auth.ts +12 −1, Explored 5 files. Use the past tense once the call has run and the plain verb before it runs or when it never ran: Run npm install. After the word Running, write the command alone. rules/content.md has the wording.
  • ds-tool-call__duration is the time elapsed while the call waits or runs, and the total once it has ended, with its unit: 42 s, 2.4 s. It is set in the interface font with figures of one width, not in mono, because a time is not code. A time that counts up is not announced: use the ds-elapsed element from behaviors/elapsed.js, or a span with aria-live="off" that the app updates.
  • A failed, declined, timed-out or cancelled call says why in one or two sentences in a span with ds-tool-call__note, the last element of the summary. It is part of the line, so it stays in view when the details are closed.
  • ds-tool-call__body holds the arguments and then the output, each under a p with ds-tool-call__label that says what it is and how long: Arguments, then Output, last 12 of 214 lines. Write both as text in a pre with ds-tool-call__code, never as markup.
  • Long output goes in ds-tool-call__output: a block that shows the last lines and scrolls inside itself. Give it role="region", aria-labelledby pointing at its label and tabindex="0", so the keyboard can scroll it. Render only the last lines, and after the block put a button with ds-button ds-button--quiet ds-show-more__all reading Show all 214 lines. When it is pressed, put every line in the same block and remove the button.
  • While a call runs, append new lines to the pre inside ds-tool-call__output. The block keeps one height and stays on its last line, so nothing around it moves. Do not make it a live region.
  • The app sets the open attribute on the details element while the call awaits approval and when it has failed, so the arguments or the error output are in view. Every other state starts closed. Leave the attribute alone once the reader has opened or closed the row.
  • While the call awaits approval, ds-tool-call__actions comes after the details element and holds Allow and Decline: two buttons with ds-button ds-button--small, secondary emphasis, each marked data-ds-critical and each with aria-describedby pointing at the title. Never put them inside the details element. When the reader answers, remove the actions, set the next state and move focus to the row's summary.
  • Announce a request for approval, a failure and the end of the run from the one status region of the view, as the activity announcer describes. The row itself is not a live region.
